en: One should lay down the thread there according to the proper rite upon the leveled ground—
[the thread] consisting of the five gnoses, pure, coiled, without knots, and extending upward from the navel.
Endowed with meditative concentration, the excellent Guru, gazing at the center of the tip of his nose, [should ensure] stability.
With the ringing of bells, auspicious songs, the sounding of conchs, recitations, and the sounds of excellent drums and flutes;

Then, the *thig* (lines) should be struck upon a ground made level by means of an excellent ritual; [the lines] are the pure nature of the five wisdoms, gathered together and without knots, abiding above the navel. Possessing stable meditative concentration, one should gaze with the eyes at the center of the tip of the nose of the sublime Guru.
They sang auspicious songs and sounded the resonance of bells, conch shells, and small drums while offering praises.

One should cause the donor to offer an *argha*—bright with fully blossomed flowers mixed with water drawn up by sprout-like hands through the hollows of the fingers—and consisting of gems, gold, and fragrant flowers.
One should also examine the omens; if the thread is severed, it indicates the death of the Guru.
Surely the death of the master will occur due to the howling of jackals, vultures, and herons.

I, the donor, shall offer the water for the arghya—scented and resembling excellent golden flowers in full, radiant bloom—blended with water taken in the lotus-petal hands of a female artisan. Furthermore, the signs must be carefully examined: if the marking-thread should snap, the preceptor will die.
If a jackal and a vulture were to cry out together, the master will certainly die.
Whatever kind of specific being has produced [the sin] by which the thread is transgressed, a bone of that same kind will certainly be found there in the subterranean site beneath the thread;
for whatever name the donor might utter while standing beside the stretched-out thread, [that is what will appear].
The surface of the bones of the beings following his name [is found] upon the fragment of earth situated at the donor.

When sentient beings born of a particular lineage have become accustomed to the ritual cord, their bones will certainly remain in that lineage beneath the ground where the cord was laid; and the donor, having approached the side, shall clearly proclaim the name of whoever [performed] the laying of the cord.
The beings who follow his name [reside] upon a fragment of earth where the donor Khaṅ-ru resides.
Or he quickly touches his own limb by the power of fate; that is the measure [of the lifespan].
This has been declared as a manifold omen for digging, but here it is stated only in brief:
a cow, having arrived, then produced dung; that is the measure of the gold situated there.
Or whatever a young girl might release, that would be silver of the same measure.

If one touches one's own body, according to the ritual empowerment, one should quickly dig [the site] to that same depth. Furthermore, regarding the many signs of the presence of minerals mentioned here, this is merely a summary: first, if a cow comes and voids its dung, gold is found at that depth; and if a child or a young girl subsequently voids [their excrement], silver is found at that depth.

The sound of frogs in the house portends danger from water; smoke portends being overwhelmed by anxiety; and seeing a woman afflicted by disease, deprived of limbs, or overcome by leprosy, one suffers illness.
The jīvañjīvaka, peacock, cuckoo, parrot, cakravāka, swan, and rṣabha— [Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly. The translation reflects the portion available.]
Their cry from the throat brings about auspicious results, and their very sight brings about perfect success.

From the croaking of frogs, there is fear of water in the house; from smoke, mental anguish; from a leper, physical decay; and from a woman, a lack of self-control. Upon seeing her, one becomes afflicted with disease. And from the cries of the *śaṃśāṇḍa*, the peacock, the cuckoo, the parrot, the *ngur ba*, and the swan...
Seeing those with throats that resonate, one's virtue increases and prosperity is brought about.
From the sounds of a lion, a rain-cloud, a king, or an elephant, there arises the attainment of grain, wealth, and prosperity;
from the auspicious sounds of children playing with conch shells, there is the arrival of riches in that house;
and from [the sounds of] an umbrella, a lotus, the sky, a water-jar, a banner, a jar, ornaments, or a royal woman—
Victory to those who are filled with the flames of fish, milk, curd, wine, and fire!

From the sounds of a lion, a rain-cloud, or an elephant, one gains wealth and grain increases; from the sounds of a conch or auspiciousness while children are playing, riches will come to that person’s home. From the sounds of a parasol, a lotus, the sky, a sprout, a banner, a vase, ornaments, or a king’s consort—
He is victorious over butter, milk, curd, honey, wine, blazing fire, and fruits.

There shall be incomparable increase in grain, wealth, sons, and so forth; when the work is completed, one partakes in the merit upon being seen by monks, Brahmins, the wise, and the most excellent people.
This applies at the commencement, during the rite of laying the foundation lines on the ground, and in the installation of deities and other such figures.
Having observed this sign of excellence, which brings about beneficial results, one should then act accordingly.

When his grain, wealth, children, and so forth had increased, and he had fully accomplished his incomparable activities, at that time the wise and wealthy brahmin monk, upon seeing virtuous people, engaged in the ritual of drawing lines upon the earth and duly arranged the deities.
At that time, these supreme signs should be thoroughly examined, for they cause benefit to increase.

Having thoroughly examined it at the outset for the sake of welfare and the arising of merit— just as [one would examine] the site of a king or a donor— the King, through artisans and teachers who were exceedingly clever in their deliberation, completely abandoned all that was inauspicious; and having first investigated it thus, he ensured it would lead to the highest well-being.
Let the undertaking be commenced on an auspicious day, joined with a favorable yoga and a benefic planet.

The artisan, a master endowed with discernment, beautiful and skillful, having completely abandoned all unwholesome acts, first performed a most thorough examination for the sake of auspiciousness and the increase of virtue, just as one would for the kings and patrons residing in all those locations.
One should properly undertake one's activities on auspicious days, during favorable conjunctions of the constellations and planets, and under the influence of the Sun.
Thus ends the procedure for the signs of casting the thread for the earth-pins.
Thus ends the ritual for marking the signs for drawing the lines on the clearing away [of obstacles].
